answers.why: Israel is given to robbers because they disobeyed God's law.
God addresses the redeemed nation as Jacob and Israel and promises protection.
The Holy One of Israel saves the nation, giving other nations for its ransom.
The Holy One of Israel addresses a plural audience whose redemption involves Babylon.
God calls himself Israel's creator and the plural audience's King.
Israel is the people formed for God in the preceding verse, reproached for neglecting worship.
Israel suffers reproach alongside the profaning of the sanctuary's princes.
Israel is addressed as God's chosen servant, parallel to the collective name Jesurun.
Taking Israel's name expresses belonging to God's people.
Jacob and Israel name God's servant nation, called to return after its sins are forgiven.
God reassures the same servant nation Israel that it will not be forgotten.
God is glorified in Israel through the redemption of his people.
